findings.title: CLAUDE.md "Follow-ups" describes an already-completed migration; line refs point past EOF
findings.description: The "Follow-ups" section says to "Migrate `_duckdb_bind_hugeint`/`_uhugeint`/`_interval` to `_call_lib_func`" and cites "Three hand-rolled intrinsics at `ducklib.py:1525-1640` (~116 lines)". In origin/main this is already done: ducklib.py is only 1431 lines (the cited 1525-1640 range does not exist), and `duckdb_bind_hugeint` (ducklib.py:1410), `duckdb_bind_uhugeint` (1416), `duckdb_bind_interval` (1422) and `duckdb_bind_decimal` (1428) are all ordinary `@cres` + `_call_lib_func` wrappers identical to the 18 sibling bind wrappers. `grep` for `intrinsic`, `_duckdb_bind_hugeint`, `_build_packed_interval` over ducklib.py returns nothing.
findings.impact: A developer following CLAUDE.md will look for ~116 lines of intrinsics at a nonexistent location and a pending migration that is already complete, wasting time and undermining trust in the doc. The cited line range past EOF makes the reference unfollowable.
findings.recommendation: Delete the "Follow-ups" section (or replace with a one-line note that hugeint/uhugeint/interval/decimal binds now route through `_call_lib_func`). Confirm numbox's `_call_lib_func` indeed handles the interval eightbyte repack before removing all mention.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md "Struct-by-value helpers (ducklib.py)" lists helpers/intrinsics that do not exist in ducklib.py
findings.description: The section states "`ducklib.py` provides" `_call_lib_func_struct_in`, `_call_lib_func_struct_out`, `_call_lib_func_byval`, `_emit_byval_call`, and `_build_packed_interval`, and that "Custom `@intrinsic` functions are used for >16-byte structs (decimal 24B, varint 24B) and interval". None of these exist in ducklib.py: there are zero local `def _*` helpers, zero `@intrinsic`, and no `_build_packed_interval`/`_call_lib_func_struct_*`/`_emit_byval_call`. The only by-value helper actually used is `_call_lib_func_byval`, which is imported from numbox (`from numbox.core.bindings.call import _call_lib_func, _call_lib_func_byval`, ducklib.py:2) and is used in just 3 places (duckdb_fetch_chunk:945, duckdb_result_return_type:1131, duckdb_result_statement_type:1137).
findings.impact: Misleading architecture documentation: it attributes a substantial ABI-lowering surface to ducklib.py that lives entirely in numbox (or was removed). Anyone debugging struct-by-value ABI will search ducklib.py in vain.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the section to reflect reality: ducklib.py defines no struct helpers or intrinsics; all by-value/struct ABI lowering is delegated to numbox's `_call_lib_func`/`_call_lib_func_byval`. Move the ABI rationale (eightbyte repack, byval+optnone) into numbox docs where the code lives, and cross-link.

findings.title: Each wrapper restates the C function name three times with no guard against drift
findings.description: All 193 wrappers follow one shape: `@cres(signatures.get("NAME"))` / `def NAME(...)` / `return _call_lib_func("NAME", (...))`. The literal function name appears three times (decorator key, def name, call string) plus once in the registration block at the top, and the docstring URL is built by hand. A typo in the `_call_lib_func("...")` string that diverges from the def name (or from a registered signature) would not be caught by any local check; it would surface only as a runtime lookup failure. (Verified all 190 currently match.) The body is otherwise pure boilerplate: ~190 functions x 4 lines that could in principle be generated by iterating the `signatures` dict.
findings.impact: Maintenance cost and a latent silent-mismatch hazard; the file is ~1431 lines that are almost entirely mechanical, raising review burden and merge-conflict surface.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) keep the explicit form but add a tiny test that asserts, for every wrapper, that the `_call_lib_func` string literal equals the def name and is a registered signature key; or (b) generate wrappers from the signatures dict via a factory. Note (b) trades away the per-function docstring links that CLAUDE.md mandates, so (a) is the lower-risk fix.

findings.title: varint wrappers use a docstring URL format that violates the project's own convention
findings.description: `duckdb_create_varint` (ducklib.py:727) and `duckdb_get_varint` (ducklib.py:1052) link to `https://duckdb.org/docs/1.3/clients/c/api#duckdb_create_varint` — a versioned path without the `.html` segment. CLAUDE.md "Adding a New Binding" step 5 mandates `https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/clients/c/api.html#func_name`, which every other wrapper uses. The two varint links are the only deviations.
findings.impact: Inconsistent/pinned-to-old-version doc links; minor but exactly the kind of drift the binding checklist exists to prevent.
findings.recommendation: Change both to the mandated `https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/clients/c/api.html#duckdb_create_varint` / `#duckdb_get_varint` form, or codify the exception if intentional (varint is version-gated via `@cres_if_available`).

notes: ducklib.py (origin/main, 1431 lines) contains exactly 193 wrappers: 190 via `_call_lib_func` + 3 via `_call_lib_func_byval` (duckdb_fetch_chunk, duckdb_result_return_type, duckdb_result_statement_type); 190 `@cres` + 3 `@cres_if_available` (duckdb_create_varint, duckdb_get_varint, duckdb_scalar_function_set_init). There are NO `@intrinsic` definitions and NO local `_*` helper functions in the file (verified by grep + AST scan); both `_call_lib_func` and `_call_lib_func_byval` are imported from numbox. Therefore the CLAUDE.md "Struct-by-value helpers" and "Follow-ups" sections are both stale relative to actual code — the headline of this review (DES-1, DES-2). All 190 `_call_lib_func` string literals match their def names and registered signature keys (no mismatches found). OUT-OF-SCOPE FLAG for a CORR pass: `duckdb_bind_decimal` (24B duckdb_decimal) and `duckdb_bind_hugeint`/`duckdb_bind_interval` now pass structs by value through plain `_call_lib_func`, yet CLAUDE.md claims custom intrinsics were previously required for the 24B decimal/varint by-value ABI. Either numbox's `_call_lib_func` gained correct >16B / eightbyte-repack handling, or there is a latent ABI bug here; correctness of that delegation should be confirmed against numbox, but it is a CORR concern, not DES.
